findings.title: Impl Notes A5 Qualification Incomplete Enumeration
findings.body: Location: proof/TP-DMX-EMBEDDED-AUDIT-COST-CONTAINMENT-001/implementation-notes.md:2384. The 'A5 successor qualification' section correctly states that A7/A9 successors modified the reusable Gemini workflows (target-validation step, new workflow_call inputs, changed checkout ref, reduced MCP tool list in gemini-review.yml) and correctly supersedes the earlier 'inspect-only' claim. However the enumeration is not exhaustive: it omits that gemini-invoke.yml also lost an MCP tool (add_issue_comment), that gemini-triage.yml's entire label-application job (issues/pull-requests write permissions) was removed, and that permissions on issues/pull-requests were reduced from write to read across gemini-invoke.yml, gemini-plan-execute.yml, gemini-triage.yml, and gemini-review.yml. This does not misrepresent history (all omitted items make the workflows more restrictive, not less), but a reader relying on the qualification's list to gauge total change scope would undercount it. Required action: Optionally broaden the qualification's bullet list to reference the permission-scope reduction and the label-job removal, or state explicitly that the listed items are illustrative rather than exhaustive.

findings.title: Settlement Preflight Fallback Reason Misleading
findings.body: Location: .github/workflows/embedded-audit.yml:329. Carried over from the prior audit and independently re-confirmed as still present and unrelated to this diff's sole content change. When the 'Review settlement preflight' step fails because scripts/audit/review_settlement.py returns non-zero for a legitimate BLOCKED settlement (active changes-requested, unresolved threads, incomplete pagination, etc. -- not because the evaluator file is missing), no SETTLEMENT_PREFLIGHT_UNAVAILABLE.txt marker is written. The diagnostic-emission logic falls back to the generic reason 'Requested PR head SHA could not be fetched or no longer matches the PR head.', which misattributes a legitimate review-settlement block to a head-fetch/staleness problem. Required action: Capture and surface the actual review_settlement.py stdout/reasons (or its exit semantics) in the fallback diagnostic path instead of reusing the head-mismatch string for settlement-caused failures.

findings.title: Pyproject Dcp Package Scope Note
findings.body: Location: pyproject.toml:173. Carried over from the prior audit and re-confirmed: pyproject.toml's sole change in this diff adds 'dopemux.dcp' to the packages list, a scope item unrelated to the embedded-audit/PR-steward/review-settlement feature this diff otherwise implements. It is now covered by test_built_wheel_runs_pr_steward_and_materializes_templates_off_tree, which asserts declared dcp packages exactly match the on-disk dcp package census. Required action: None required; note for traceability only.

findings.title: Successor Single Commit Claim Unverifiable
findings.body: successor_note asserts subject_head adds 'exactly one documentation-only commit' on top of prior_audited_head. frozen.diff is a base_at_freeze..subject_head diff (32 files, matching changed-files.txt), not a prior_audited_head..subject_head diff, and no commit log/per-commit diff was supplied. implementation-notes.md itself is 'new file mode 100644' against base_at_freeze, so this diff cannot show which lines within that file were introduced by which commit. The claim that only implementation-notes.md changed between prior_audited_head and subject_head cannot be independently confirmed from the supplied artifacts alone. Required action: If exact commit-boundary verification is required, supply `git log prior_audited_head..subject_head --stat` or an equivalent per-commit diff alongside frozen.diff in future audit packages.

fixes_applied: R1's BLOCKING wheel-completeness finding empirically disproven via real uv build --wheel + wheel-member inspection + pytest of test_built_wheel_runs_pr_steward_and_materializes_templates_off_tree (1 passed); no pyproject.toml change required or made.
R1's MEDIUM implementation-notes finding repaired: added an explicit A5 successor qualification and relabeled document status as a historical ledger, preserving original chronology.
remaining_risks: Wheel completeness for the two new template workflow files (and other packaged non-.py assets) is supported by a new build-and-inspect regression test (test_built_wheel_runs_pr_steward_and_materializes_templates_off_tree) that builds a real wheel via `uv build --wheel` and asserts required members are present, but this audit session cannot execute candidate/build code, and MANIFEST.in plus the full tool.setuptools.include-package-data configuration are not visible anywhere in frozen.diff (unchanged, and not shown as context). The prior BLOCKING wheel-completeness finding is very likely resolved based on this structural test evidence, but that conclusion rests partly on the (unverified-in-session) claim that the build+test were run externally and passed.
The 'exactly one documentation-only commit' successor scoping claim rests on git history not provided to this audit; only the net base..head diff was reviewable.

Broad functional review (embedded-audit.yml, pr-steward.yml, review_settlement.py, readiness invalidator/writer, Gemini reusable workflows) was performed via targeted reading of a very large (6700+ line) diff rather than exhaustive line-by-line review of every unchanged-vs-prior-audit code path; spot checks found no defects, but full re-derivation of every branch was out of scope given this successor audit's narrow binding to a documentation-only change.
